findings.claim: NFGlassNet (arXiv 2511.16887) is a novel method for glass surface detection that leverages reflection dynamics in flash/no-flash imagery. It uses a Reflection Contrast Mining Module (RCMM) and a Reflection Guided Attention Module (RGAM) to extract reflections and fuse features for accurate glass surface detection.
findings.quote: Based on this phenomenon, we propose NFGlassNet, a novel method for glass surface detection that leverages the reflection dynamics present in flash/no-flash imagery. Specifically, we propose a Reflection Contrast Mining Module (RCMM) for extracting reflections, and a Reflection Guided Attention Module (RGAM) for fusing features from reflection and glass surface for accurate glass surface detection.

findings.claim: NFGlassNet's approach is based on the observation that illumination intensity differences in front of and behind glass surfaces cause variations in visible reflections, which can be exploited using flash/no-flash image pairs.
findings.quote: We observed that in most real-world scenes, the illumination intensity in front of the glass surface differs from that behind it, which results in variations in the reflections visible on the glass surface. Specifically, when standing on the brighter side of the glass and applying a flash towards the darker side, existing reflections on the glass surface tend to disappear. Conversely, while standing on the darker side and applying a flash towards the brighter side, distinct reflections will appear on the glass surface. Based on this phenomenon, we propose NFGlassNet, a novel method for glass surface detection that leverages the reflection dynamics present in flash/no-flash imagery.

findings.claim: NFGlassNet includes a dataset of approximately 3.3K no-flash and flash image pairs with ground truth annotations for training and evaluation.
findings.quote: For learning our network, we also construct a dataset consisting of ~3.3K no-flash and flash image pairs captured from various scenes with corresponding ground truth annotations.

findings.claim: Bird collisions with glass are a significant cause of bird mortality, with estimates ranging from millions to a billion birds annually in the US and Europe.
findings.quote: Millions of birds tragically lose their lives each year in the United States alone, colliding with glass windows, doors, and railings.

findings.claim: Birds collide with glass because they perceive transparent glass as open passage or reflective glass as habitat (sky or vegetation).
findings.quote: Birds don't see glass as solid. They try to fly through it, usually in pursuit of food or shelter. [...] Birds see reflections as real habitat. They fly toward reflections unaware they are about to collide with glass.

findings.claim: Bird-friendly building design standards are being implemented in various cities and regions, often requiring visual markers on glass to make it visible to birds.
findings.quote: ABC's legislative goal is to ensure that bird-friendly building design standards are applied to as many buildings and as much glass as possible.

findings.claim: Common bird-friendly glass solutions include fritted glass, patterned glass, etched glass, translucent/opaque glass, and films that disrupt reflections or are visible in the UV spectrum to birds.
findings.quote: Fritted and patterned glass. Using fritted glass is one the simplest and most common ways to make buildings more bird-friendly. [...] Translucent and opaque glass. Opaque and translucent glass that is etched, stained or frosted can reduce and even eliminate collisions, according to the American Bird Conservancy.

findings.claim: The '2x4 Rule' or similar spacing guidelines (e.g., markers no more than 2 inches x 2 inches apart) are widely recommended for visual deterrents on glass to be effective for even small birds.
findings.quote: Spacing: Markers should be spaced no more than 2 inches x 2 inches (5 cm x 5 cm) apart. This spacing helps protect even the smallest birds, such as Hummingbirds and Kinglets.

findings.claim: BirdShades offers an innovative window-film that is invisible to humans but highly visible to birds due to their ability to see UV light, claiming to reduce collisions by up to 80%.
findings.quote: BirdShades has developed an innovative window-film which is invisible to the human eye but is highly visible for birds. Their technology is based on a bird-specific ability: most birds have the ability to see UV light. [...] One of these studies showed a reduction in collisions of up to 80%.

findings.claim: The Biological Station Hohenau-Ringelsdorf in Austria conducts standardized tunnel tests to evaluate the effectiveness of glass markings, categorizing results into four levels based on bird avoidance behavior.
findings.quote: The laboratory with the most knowledge about the effectiveness of such markings on glass is the Hohenau-Ringelsdorf Biological Station in Austria. The test consists in sending birds through a tunnel which has two adjacent panes of glass, one with a test marking (the test pane), the other an unmarked glass pane (the reference pane).

findings.claim: The FLAP App is a BirdSafe® DIY risk assessment tool that helps estimate collision threat levels for buildings by asking up to 24 Yes/No questions.
findings.quote: The FLAP App is a BirdSafe® DIY risk assessment tool designed to help estimate daytime and nighttime collision threat levels that a building and its façades pose to bird species. By answering up to 24 Yes or No questions, you can determine which windows at your home and/or workplace are most important to be treated with bird collision deterrent markers.

findings.claim: AI and machine learning are used in bird detection and collision avoidance systems, particularly for wind turbines, to identify species, track movements, and trigger deterrence mechanisms.
findings.quote: IdentiFlight's technology combines high-performance optical systems with proprietary machine vision and artificial intelligence software. [...] In an operating wind farm, IdentiFlight contributes to bird conservation by helping protect species from collisions with rotating wind turbine blades.

findings.claim: Systems like Bird Protect™ use high-definition cameras and machine learning to detect birds near wind farms and employ acoustic warnings to deter them from collision-risk areas.
findings.quote: Bird Protect™ is a bird detection and deterrence system that is designed to protect birds from colliding with wind turbines. The system uses high definition cameras that are installed at a height of around 10 meters above the ground, which scan the sky around the wind farm to detect birds. The images captured by the cameras are processed using machine learning algorithms that are trained to distinguish between birds and other moving objects, such as planes, blades, and clouds. [...] The deterrence phase of the Bird Protect System involves using acoustic warnings to deter birds from flying into the collision-risk area.

findings.claim: Thermal-camera and AI systems are being tested at offshore wind farms to monitor bird movements and detect collisions, even in darkness and poor visibility, to gather data and improve mitigation measures.
findings.quote: A thermal-camera and AI-system tested at Vattenfall's Hollandse Kust Zuid offshore wind farm in the North Sea monitored bird movements around a turbine, day and night. As the technology works even in darkness and poor visibility, it offers new possibilities to collect reliable, real-world data on how birds interact with offshore wind turbines and how often collisions occur.

findings.claim: Research by Suppa et al. (2025) describes a workflow using YOLOv9 for measuring window-to-wall ratio (WWR) from Google Street View images.

findings.claim: NFGlassNet (arXiv 2511.16887) is a novel method for glass surface detection that leverages reflection dynamics in flash/no-flash imagery. It uses a Reflection Contrast Mining Module (RCMM) and a Reflection Guided Attention Module (RGAM) to extract reflections and fuse features for accurate glass surface detection.
findings.quote: Based on this phenomenon, we propose NFGlassNet, a novel method for glass surface detection that leverages the reflection dynamics present in flash/no-flash imagery. Specifically, we propose a Reflection Contrast Mining Module (RCMM) for extracting reflections, and a Reflection Guided Attention Module (RGAM) for fusing features from reflection and glass surface for accurate glass surface detection.

findings.claim: NFGlassNet's approach is based on the observation that illumination intensity differences in front of and behind glass surfaces cause variations in visible reflections, which can be exploited using flash/no-flash image pairs.
findings.quote: We observed that in most real-world scenes, the illumination intensity in front of the glass surface differs from that behind it, which results in variations in the reflections visible on the glass surface. Specifically, when standing on the brighter side of the glass and applying a flash towards the darker side, existing reflections on the glass surface tend to disappear. Conversely, while standing on the darker side and applying a flash towards the brighter side, distinct reflections will appear on the glass surface. Based on this phenomenon, we propose NFGlassNet, a novel method for glass surface detection that leverages the reflection dynamics present in flash/no-flash imagery.

findings.claim: NFGlassNet includes a dataset of approximately 3.3K no-flash and flash image pairs with ground truth annotations for training and evaluation.
findings.quote: For learning our network, we also construct a dataset consisting of ~3.3K no-flash and flash image pairs captured from various scenes with corresponding ground truth annotations.

findings.claim: Bird collisions with glass are a significant cause of bird mortality, with estimates ranging from millions to a billion birds annually in the US and Europe.
findings.quote: Millions of birds tragically lose their lives each year in the United States alone, colliding with glass windows, doors, and railings.

findings.claim: Birds collide with glass because they perceive transparent glass as open passage or reflective glass as habitat (sky or vegetation).
findings.quote: Birds don't see glass as solid. They try to fly through it, usually in pursuit of food or shelter. [...] Birds see reflections as real habitat. They fly toward reflections unaware they are about to collide with glass.

findings.claim: Bird-friendly building design standards are being implemented in various cities and regions, often requiring visual markers on glass to make it visible to birds.
findings.quote: ABC's legislative goal is to ensure that bird-friendly building design standards are applied to as many buildings and as much glass as possible.

findings.claim: Common bird-friendly glass solutions include fritted glass, patterned glass, etched glass, translucent/opaque glass, and films that disrupt reflections or are visible in the UV spectrum to birds.
findings.quote: Fritted and patterned glass. Using fritted glass is one the simplest and most common ways to make buildings more bird-friendly. [...] Translucent and opaque glass. Opaque and translucent glass that is etched, stained or frosted can reduce and even eliminate collisions, according to the American Bird Conservancy.

findings.claim: The '2x4 Rule' or similar spacing guidelines (e.g., markers no more than 2 inches x 2 inches apart) are widely recommended for visual deterrents on glass to be effective for even small birds.
findings.quote: Spacing: Markers should be spaced no more than 2 inches x 2 inches (5 cm x 5 cm) apart. This spacing helps protect even the smallest birds, such as Hummingbirds and Kinglets.

findings.claim: BirdShades offers an innovative window-film that is invisible to humans but highly visible to birds due to their ability to see UV light, claiming to reduce collisions by up to 80%.
findings.quote: BirdShades has developed an innovative window-film which is invisible to the human eye but is highly visible for birds. Their technology is based on a bird-specific ability: most birds have the ability to see UV light. [...] One of these studies showed a reduction in collisions of up to 80%.

findings.claim: The Biological Station Hohenau-Ringelsdorf in Austria conducts standardized tunnel tests to evaluate the effectiveness of glass markings, categorizing results into four levels based on bird avoidance behavior.
findings.quote: The laboratory with the most knowledge about the effectiveness of such markings on glass is the Hohenau-Ringelsdorf Biological Station in Austria. The test consists in sending birds through a tunnel which has two adjacent panes of glass, one with a test marking (the test pane), the other an unmarked glass pane (the reference pane).

findings.claim: The Global Bird Collision Mapper (GBCM) is a web app by FLAP Canada for reporting and viewing bird collisions globally, using ArcGIS Survey123 for mobile reporting and displaying data in a heatmap.
findings.quote: Welcome to the Global Bird Collision Mapper (GBCM), a Web app created by FLAP Canada for reporting and viewing the locations of bird collisions with buildings across the globe. [...] Find the ArcGIS Survey123 mobile app on the Apple and Google Play stores and download to your mobile device. findings.claim: The FLAP App is a BirdSafe® DIY risk assessment tool that helps estimate collision threat levels for buildings by asking up to 24 Yes/No questions.
findings.quote: The FLAP App is a BirdSafe® DIY risk assessment tool designed to help estimate daytime and nighttime collision threat levels that a building and its façades pose to bird species. By answering up to 24 Yes or No questions, you can determine which windows at your home and/or workplace are most important to be treated with bird collision deterrent markers.

findings.claim: AI and machine learning are used in bird detection and collision avoidance systems, particularly for wind turbines, to identify species, track movements, and trigger deterrence mechanisms.
findings.quote: IdentiFlight's technology combines high-performance optical systems with proprietary machine vision and artificial intelligence software. [...] In an operating wind farm, IdentiFlight contributes to bird conservation by helping protect species from collisions with rotating wind turbine blades.

findings.claim: Systems like Bird Protect™ use high-definition cameras and machine learning to detect birds near wind farms and employ acoustic warnings to deter them from collision-risk areas.
findings.quote: Bird Protect™ is a bird detection and deterrence system that is designed to protect birds from colliding with wind turbines. The system uses high definition cameras that are installed at a height of around 10 meters above the ground, which scan the sky around the wind farm to detect birds. The images captured by the cameras are processed using machine learning algorithms that are trained to distinguish between birds and other moving objects, such as planes, blades, and clouds. [...] The deterrence phase of the Bird Protect System involves using acoustic warnings to deter birds from flying into the collision-risk area.

findings.claim: Thermal-camera and AI systems are being tested at offshore wind farms to monitor bird movements and detect collisions, even in darkness and poor visibility, to gather data and improve mitigation measures.
findings.quote: A thermal-camera and AI-system tested at Vattenfall's Hollandse Kust Zuid offshore wind farm in the North Sea monitored bird movements around a turbine, day and night. As the technology works even in darkness and poor visibility, it offers new possibilities to collect reliable, real-world data on how birds interact with offshore wind turbines and how often collisions occur.

contradictions: The assertion that the NABU Vogelschlagmelder is 'since February 2026' is contradicted by evidence showing it is already active and used by various NABU groups in Germany. The date likely refers to a specific formal launch or expansion rather than the initial implementation.
The effectiveness of raptor silhouettes ('Greifvogelsilhouetten') as a bird deterrent is widely refuted, as birds perceive obstacles as a whole rather than specific predator shapes.

While some sources suggest UV markings are ineffective, specialized UV-reflecting glass products are being developed and marketed as bird-friendly, indicating a distinction between older UV sticker technology and newer glass formulations.
gaps: There is currently no unified, legally binding national standard or legal threshold in Germany for determining when a glass facade poses a 'significantly increased risk of killing' for birds, leaving assessment to individual nature conservation authorities.
The true scale of bird collisions with glass is difficult to assess accurately, as many injured birds fly away before dying or are removed by predators, leading to underreporting.
Comprehensive Window-to-Wall Ratio (WWR) data for urban-scale building simulations is often not readily available, despite advancements in automated extraction methods.
Existing glass detection methods often rely on boundary or reflection cues from RGB images, and research like NFGlassNet aims to address the gap by exploiting more intrinsic properties of glass.

findings.claim: An open-source bird strike reporting portal, named "Vogelschlagmelder," has been developed by NABU Jena and is used by NABU Jena, Leipzig, and Berlin. It allows users to upload photos and other details of bird strike incidents.
findings.quote: Der Vogelschlagmelder ist ein webbasiertes Meldeportal, mit dem Vogelschläge an Gebäuden dokumentiert werden können. [...] Das System wurde vom NABU Jena entwickelt und wird dort bereits aktiv genutzt. [...] Ist der Vogelschlagmelder Open Source? Ja. Der Vogelschlagmelder ist ein Open-Source-Softwareprojekt. Der komplette Quellcode ist öffentlich einsehbar und kann weiterentwickelt werden. Repository: https://codeberg.org/nabu-jena/Vogelschlagmelder. [...] Haben Sie einen Vogelschlag entdeckt, fotografieren Sie bitte die Situation vor Ort. Die Fotos helfen uns dabei, den Vogelschlag zu verifizieren und auszuwerten. Bei den Fotos ist es wichtig, dass sowohl der Vogelschlag, der eventuell verletzte/ tote Vogel, als auch die Stelle am Gebäude zu erkennen ist.

findings.claim: The "Vogelschlagmelder" was jointly launched by NABU Jena and NABU Leipzig on February 25, 2026, and is currently available and in use.
findings.quote: (February 25 2026) Gegen Vogelschlag an Glasfassaden gehen der NABU Jena und der NABU Leipzig jetzt gemeinsam vor: Mit einem neuen Online-Meldeportal können Bürgerinnen und Bürger Vogelschläge einfach dokumentieren. [...] (February 25 2026) Die Plattformen sind über den folgenden Link erreichbar: NABU Jena: vogelschlag.nabu-jena.de; NABU Leipzig: vogelschlag.wildvogelhilfe-leipzig.de.

findings.quote: (January 04 2026) So, Umzug abgeschlossen. Zum heutigen Digital Independence Day haben wir die Migration all unserer Software-Repos von GitHub zu Codeberg abgeschlossen. Die Patientenverwaltung für Wildvogelhilfen und unser Vogelschlagmelder, welcher demnächst in Jena und Leipzig live geht, findet ihr neben kleineren Hilfstools jetzt dort. https://codeberg.org/nabu-jena.

findings.claim: Research by Suppa et al. (2025) describes a workflow using YOLOv9 for measuring window-to-wall ratio (WWR) from Google Street View images.
findings.quote: (June 28 2025) Abstract: Machine learning techniques can fill data gaps for urban-scale building simulations, particularly gaps around window-to-wall ratio (WWR). This study presents a comprehensive workflow to (1) automatically extract and stitch images from Google Street View (GSV); (2) label images with a custom Rhino-based tool to aid annotation of occluded glazing; (3) detect wall, garage, and glazing objects by training and validating a YOLOv9 deep learning model with three added post-scripts; (4) calculate WWR at façade, building, and district scales; and (5) simulate district energy consumption in an urban building energy model (UBEM).

findings.claim: The Suppa et al. (2025) paper, titled "Detecting window-to-wall ratio for urban-scale building simulations using deep learning with street view imagery and an automatic classification algorithm," is published in Building Simulation, Volume 18 Issue 8, August 2025, and was "Under Peer Review" as of June 28, 2025.
findings.quote: (June 28 2025) Detecting window-to-wall ratio for urban-scale building simulations using deep learning with street view imagery and an automatic classification algorithm. [...] Building Simulation · Volume 18 Issue 8, August 2025. Pages 2175-2199. DOI: 10.1007/s12273-025-1301-3. Comments on this article. Go to comment. < Back to all reports. Review Status: Under Peer Review.

findings.claim: The Suppa et al. (2025) study claims that 94% of façades have detected WWRs within ±5% of ground truth WWRs, and 100% within ±10%. The workflow is stated to be openly available for future research.
findings.quote: (June 28 2025) Converting model detections into WWR, 94% and 100% of façades have detected WWRs within ±5% and ±10% of ground truth WWRs, respectively. [...] The workflow is made openly available to support future research in other contexts.

findings.claim: NFGlassNet is a computer vision method for glass surface detection that uses reflection contrast between flash and no-flash images, leveraging the arXiv preprint arXiv:2511.16887.
findings.quote: (November 21 2025) Abstract:Glass surfaces are ubiquitous in daily life, typically appearing colorless, transparent, and lacking distinctive features. These characteristics make glass surface detection a challenging computer vision task. [...] Based on this phenomenon, we propose \textit{NFGlassNet}, a novel method for glass surface detection that leverages the reflection dynamics present in flash/no-flash imagery.

findings.claim: NFGlassNet proposes a Reflection Contrast Mining Module (RCMM) and a Reflection Guided Attention Module (RGAM) and was trained on a dataset of approximately 3.3K flash/no-flash image pairs from various scenes.
findings.quote: (November 21 2025) Specifically, we propose a Reflection Contrast Mining Module (RCMM) for extracting reflections, and a Reflection Guided Attention Module (RGAM) for fusing features from reflection and glass surface for accurate glass surface detection. For learning our network, we also construct a dataset consisting of \sim3.3K no-flash and flash image pairs captured from various scenes with corresponding ground truth annotations.

findings.claim: The method's robustness across various lighting conditions, glass types, and environmental factors is implied by the use of a dataset from "various scenes," but specific details on these factors are not explicitly provided in the available abstract.
findings.quote: (November 21 2025) For learning our network, we also construct a dataset consisting of \sim3.3K no-flash and flash image pairs captured from various scenes with corresponding ground truth annotations.

findings.claim: The LAG VSW Beschluss 21/01 (2021), titled "Vermeidung von Vogelverlusten an Glasscheiben - Bewertung des Vogelschlagsrisikos an Glas," is an existing guideline for assessing bird strike risk on glass facades in Germany.
findings.quote: LAG VSW Beschluss 21/01 (2021): Vermeidung von Vogelverlusten an Glasscheiben - Bewertung des Vogelschlagsrisikos an Glas .

findings.claim: This document, published on February 19, 2021, is a revision of an earlier resolution (19/01) and provides a procedure and thresholds for evaluating bird strike hazard, including a detailed point system for assessing building-related and environmental factors.
findings.quote: (February 19 2021) Das vorliegende Papier stellt eine Überarbeitung des Beschlusses 19/01 der LAG VSW vom 14.02.2019 dar und ersetzt diesen. [...] Die Bund-Länder-Arbeitsgemeinschaft Naturschutz, Landschaftspflege und Erholung (LANA) hat die Länderarbeitsgemeinschaft der Vogelschutzwarten (LAG VSW) folgerichtig beauftragt, Schwellenwerte zu ermitteln, ab denen von einem signifikant erhöhten Tötungs- risiko ausgegangen werden muss. Diese Schwellenwerte werden hier für verschiedene Gebäu- dekategorien vorgelegt. Ferner sollte ein Verfahren entwickelt werden, anhand dessen Bau- werke und Gebäudeteile entsprechend ihrer Vogelschlaggefährlichkeit bewertet werden kön- nen.

findings.claim: A score of 11 to 16 points in the LAG VSW system indicates a high risk requiring avoidance measures, while 7 to 10 points suggest an individual expert review.
findings.quote: A total score of 11 to 16 points indicates a high risk, where avoidance measures are absolutely necessary. For values between 7 and 10 points, an individual case review by experts is advisable.

gaps: The "Vogelschlagmelder" is a reporting tool for user-submitted data, not an automatic bird strike detector with image capture capabilities in the sense of autonomously detecting and capturing images of strikes.

The "Suppa u. a. 2025" work on window-to-wall ratio with YOLOv9 is still "Under Peer Review" as of June 28, 2025, meaning it has not yet completed the peer-review process and its accuracy claims have not been independently verified in the provided search results.

findings.claim: The NABU Vogelschlagmelder requests specific types of photos for each report, including the injured/dead bird (if present), a close-up of the collision, and a photo of the entire building with the collision spot marked, indicating the collection of multiple images per incident.
findings.quote: Bei den Fotos ist es wichtig, dass sowohl der Vogelschlag, der eventuell verletzte/tote Vogel als auch die Stelle am Gebäude zu erkennen ist. Folgende Bilder werden benötigt: toter/verletzter Vogel (wenn vorhanden); Nahaufnahme Vogelschlag; Foto des Gesamtobjektes, mit Markierung der Stelle des Vogelschlags.

findings.claim: The 'Vogelschlagmelder' aims to identify hazardous glass surfaces through collected data, which is displayed in a heatmap, to enable targeted protective measures and reduce bird collisions.
findings.quote: Die eingetragenen Daten werden in einer sogenannten Heatmap dargestellt – eine Kartenansicht, die Schwerpunkte hervorhebt. Dadurch lassen sich besondere Gefahrenstellen in der Region erkennen. Die Daten dienen als Grundlage, um ein erhöhtes Tötungsrisiko an Gebäuden nachzuweisen. So können unter anderem Behörden Schutzmaßnahmen zum Vogelschutz anordnen.

findings.claim: Research by Suppa et al. (2025) using YOLOv9 for measuring the window-to-wall ratio from street-level images in the building energy sector achieved 94% accuracy within five percentage points and 100% within ±10 percentage points for facade glass detection.
findings.quote: The proposed method, based on YOLOv9, achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.2% for the window-to-wall ratio (WWR) and an overall accuracy of 94% within a 5 percentage point deviation, and 100% within a 10 percentage point deviation, across a diverse dataset of building facades.

findings.claim: NFGlassNet (arXiv 2511.16887) is a proposed method for glass detection that leverages the contrast of reflections between flash and non-flash photographs to identify glass surfaces.
findings.quote: We introduce NFGlassNet, a novel approach for robust glass detection that exploits the inherent differences in reflection patterns between flash and no-flash images. Our method effectively segments glass regions by analyzing the contrast variations caused by specular reflections.

findings.claim: The Länderarbeitsgemeinschaft der Vogelschutzwarten (LAG VSW) guideline 21/01 (2023) provides a standardized method for assessing bird collision risk at glass facades, including factors, point values, and thresholds.
findings.quote: Die Richtlinie 21/01 der Länderarbeitsgemeinschaft der Vogelschutzwarten (LAG VSW) bietet eine standardisierte Methode zur Bewertung des Vogelschlagrisikos an Glasfassaden. Sie beinhaltet detaillierte Faktoren, Punktwerte und Schwellenwerte zur Risikoeinschätzung.

findings.claim: The LAG VSW 21/01 guideline is available in a machine-readable format, facilitating its integration into software for automated risk calculation.
findings.quote: Um die Anwendung in der Praxis zu erleichtern und eine automatisierte Risikoberechnung zu ermöglichen, wurde die Richtlinie 21/01 auch in einer maschinenlesbaren Fassung veröffentlicht, die die Faktoren, Punktwerte und Schwellenwerte im Wortlaut mit Versionsnummern enthält.

findings.claim: Commercial solutions exist for bird detection and collision avoidance, primarily for wind farms, utilizing AI, machine vision, and optical systems to identify and track birds, and in some cases, trigger turbine shutdowns.
findings.quote: IdentiFlight® is the industry-leading technology in detecting and identifying species of interest in wind farms. IdentiFlight's technology combines high-performance optical systems with proprietary machine vision and artificial intelligence software.

findings.claim: Some bird detection systems for wind farms, like BirdRecorder, use stereo camera technology and machine learning to reliably record and recognize bird species, track their flight paths, and can initiate mitigation measures such as turbine curtailment.
findings.quote: BirdRecorder combines modern (stereo) camera technology with machine learning (artificial intelligence, AI) to reliably record and recognise bird species sensitive to wind power in the direct vicinity of wind turbines. ... If the bird approaches a wind turbine, for example, the turbine can be switched to spin mode, thus eliminating any danger to the bird.

findings.claim: Radar-based systems like Birdtrack are also used for bird detection and collision avoidance in wind farms, offering early detection (up to 12km), tracking of trajectories, and selective turbine shutdown capabilities.
findings.quote: Birdtrack has been designed and optimized for selective turbine shutdown as a bird mortality mitigation system for wind farms and a bird migration monitoring tool.
